jd.text:
AI基础数据标注员
【工作形式】
全程远程办公，需自备电脑及稳定网络，时间相对灵活（全职/兼职/寒暑假均可）
【项目分类与工作内容】
图文类标注：包括图片分类、物体框选、图文匹配、图文内容描述、简单画面校验等。需看懂基础画面，按规范完成标注，线上培训1-2小时即可上手。
语音类标注：包括语音转写、口音校对、情绪分类、杂音标注、方言语音校验等。需听音频并对照修正，需耳机及安静环境，普通话/方言熟练者更适配。
中小学题库标注：针对小学、初中全学科题目进行标准化处理（如文字校对、知识点标签匹配、答案解析校验、题型分类、难易度分级）。需具备中小学学习基础，能看懂基础试题。
通用文本标注：包括文案合规筛查、对话意图分类、文本情感判断、段落摘要标注、问答匹配等。需对文字敏感，阅读细致。
【招募要求】
基础条件：本科（在读）及以上，专业不限；能保证每日至少4-8小时空余标注时长。
能力适配：根据所选项目类别，需具备相应的基础能力（如文字阅读、语音辨识、基础学科知识等）。
考核要求：需通过项目评审（试标）后才能正式进项目。
【薪酬与福利】
薪酬标准：时薪约25-50元（按工时或计件结算），每月5号前结算，打入实名银行账户。
福利保障：提供线上标注培训和试标指导；合作满2个月以上可开具实习证明。
【报名与入职流程】
报名：投递简历到邮箱，简历通过有专员通知试标。入职：试标通过、签署实习协议后，正式进项目参与标注任务。
(注：该项目为线上数据标注兼职/实习，不涉及线下办公，无押金，请防范任何形式的收费陷阱）

简历投递方式：23530608@qq.com

Internship Application — Governance & Sustainable Development (GSD) 
Dear Hiring Team,
I am writing to apply for the Governance and Sustainable Development (GSD) internship at the Asia-Europe Foundation. With a trilingual profile (Chinese, English, French), a double major in English Literature and Finance, and hands-on experience liaising across UN, government, and academic institutions, I believe I can contribute to ASEF's work on Green Economy, Human Rights, and Diplomacy — and, in return, learn from the Foundation's unique Asia-Europe vantage point.
My academic path has prepared me to work at the intersection of analysis and communication that GSD projects require. English Literature trained me to write precisely across registers, from policy briefs to public-facing content, while Finance gave me the quantitative and budget-aware mindset relevant to sustainable development and green economy work. As a native Chinese speaker fluent in English (IELTS 7.5) with working French, I can engage stakeholders across ASEF's 51 partner countries.
My experience closely mirrors the department's coordination and capacity-building functions. Since April 2026, I have served as an Institutional Liaison Intern for the UN International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists (IYRP) Chinese Communication & Practice Working Group, coordinating among participating organizations, drafting and disseminating Chinese-language content on UN themes, and maintaining liaison records. In parallel, I support the China-Malaysia International Institute for Higher Education Research (Xiamen University) as an Administrative Office Assistant, coordinating between Chinese and Malaysian academic partners — the same kind of bi-regional bridging ASEF performs between Asia and Europe. Earlier, as a Project Assistant for a Ministry of Commerce foreign-aid training programme, I helped deliver capacity-building training for overseas officials and supported conference operations at the 15th China–Northeast Asia Expo.
I am drawn to ASEF's GSD Department specifically because it convenes civil society and governments in open, multisectoral dialogue — an approach I find both effective and inspiring. I would bring reliability, cross-cultural sensitivity, and a genuine commitment to the Asia-Europe partnership.
I am available for a full-time internship of three to six months and have provided my nationality, date of birth, expected graduation date (June 2028), and availability period in the application form. Thank you for considering my application; I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how I can support the GSD team.
Sincerely,
Yuan XIAO (肖媛)

To the Hiring Manager,
I am a full-time undergraduate student in English Language and Literature (minor in Finance) at Jilin University, China, expected to graduate in June 2028. I am writing to express my strong interest in the OECD Internship Programme at Headquarters in Paris, and to explain why I want to join, how I can contribute, and how the experience fits my career goals.
Why I want to join the OECD
The OECD's role in building evidence-based public-policy standards across its 38 member economies speaks directly to my aim of working at the intersection of international development and cross-border communication. I want to learn first-hand how multilateral policy is researched, negotiated, and turned into standards that raise economic and social well-being. A placement in Paris - at the centre of this multicultural, member-government-facing environment - is precisely where I hope to learn and contribute.
How I will contribute
My background maps onto the internship's three core activities - policy-research support, data work, and event organisation.
1) Bilingual communication. With IELTS 7.5 and professional working proficiency in English (native Mandarin), I can draft clear reports, briefings, and correspondence and interpret across cultures - skills tested through 12 bilingual translation sessions for MOFCOM foreign-aid programmes serving 80+ participants from 15+ countries.
2) Research and data. As first author of a sociolinguistic field study I designed surveys, coded qualitative samples, and wrote the empirical analysis; as an assistant for the UN IYRP Working Group I maintained a 100+ record expert database to strict accuracy standards. I am comfortable with Python and MySQL for data cleaning and with Microsoft Office for reporting - directly supporting the data organisation, analysis, and report writing the role requires.
3) Operational coordination. At the China-Northeast Asia Expo I coordinated foreign-guest reception for 200+ international delegates across six departments and three forums, and I have supported academic and policy forums end-to-end. I can manage logistics, scheduling, and stakeholder liaison reliably in a fast-paced, multicultural team.
How the internship advances my goals
My career aim is to contribute to international development policy and the institutions that deliver it, building on my Finance minor and my experience across BRICS, SDG, and development-cooperation programmes. The OECD internship would give me rigorous, hands-on exposure to multilateral policy research and member-government engagement, while deepening my ability to turn analysis into actionable policy language - the natural next step toward a career in international organisations or development finance.
I am available for a full-time internship, meet the English-language requirement, and am eager to learn French on site. Thank you for considering my application; I would welcome the chance to support the OECD's mission.
Sincerely,
Yuan Xiao

To the FAO Internship Programme Team,
I am writing to express my strong interest in the FAO Internship Programme at Headquarters in Rome, and specifically in the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists (IYRP) Chinese Working Group - Institutional Liaison Assistant internship. I am a full-time undergraduate student in English Language and Literature (minor in Finance) at Jilin University, China, expected to graduate in June 2028, and a national of an FAO Member State.
Why I want to join FAO
FAO's mandate - to defeat hunger, advance sustainable agri-food systems, and translate evidence into the Four Betters (Better Production, Better Nutrition, Better Environment, Better Life) - maps directly onto my academic and practical path. I want to learn how multilateral policy on food security and sustainable production is researched, negotiated, and delivered to member countries. I am especially drawn to FAO's work on rangelands and pastoralist livelihoods, which sits at the crossroads of livestock, sustainable land management, and resilient food systems.
Why my background fits this role
My most relevant experience is my assistantship with the UN International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists (IYRP) Working Group. Supporting this UN observance gave me first-hand exposure to how rangeland sustainability and pastoralist livelihoods connect to FAO's mandate. I helped maintain a 100+ record expert database and coordinated multilingual materials, work that mirrors the data organisation, monitoring, and stakeholder liaison this liaison role requires.
This is reinforced by agriculture-related studies and field exposure that grounded my understanding of food production and rural livelihoods, and by development-cooperation experience: twelve bilingual translation sessions for MOFCOM foreign-aid programmes serving 80+ participants from 15+ countries, plus involvement in BRICS and SDG initiatives. These taught me how international development cooperation operates on the ground.
A distinctive asset is language: as a native Mandarin speaker with IELTS 7.5, I command two of FAO's official languages (Chinese and English). For the IYRP Chinese Working Group, this bilingual capacity directly supports Chinese-language promotion, institutional liaison with Chinese partners, and the UNFCCC observer accreditation process, where accurate cross-language communication matters.
How I will contribute
In this Institutional Liaison Assistant role I can support the IYRP Chinese Working Group by helping prepare and track the UNFCCC observer accreditation application, drafting and translating Chinese-language promotion materials, maintaining partner and expert databases, and coordinating outreach across institutions. My skills in Python and MySQL for data cleaning, qualitative coding for structured analysis, and Microsoft Office for reporting would let me contribute to research, dashboards, and technical writing from day one. At the China-Northeast Asia Expo I coordinated foreign-guest reception for 200+ delegates across six departments, evidence that I can manage logistics and stakeholder liaison reliably in a fast-paced, multicultural team.
I am available for a full-time internship of three months and open to a longer placement, meet the working-knowledge English requirement, and am committed to FAO's zero-fee, merit-based values. Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the chance to support FAO's mission.
Sincerely,
Yuan Xiao
